newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland welcomes EU decision on telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Ireland welcomes EU decision on telecoms.

text.p: Irish telecommunications minister Michael Lowry on Wednesday welcomed a European Commission decision on dates for the liberalisation of the telecommunications sector in Ireland.

The Commission approved a timetable which allows infrastructure competitors to enter the Irish market from the middle of next year. Alternative infrastructure providers will be permitted from July 1, 1997 and full liberalisation will take place from the beginning of 2000.
Meanwhile, direct international connections for GSM mobile phone providers will be liberalised from January 1, 1999 and voice telephony will be completely liberalised from January 1, 2000.
Under the liberalisation directives, Ireland was entitled to request a derogation period up to 2003.
"This is good news first and foremost for telecommunications consumers who will see greater choice, higher quality and lower prices starting from next year," Lowry said in a statement.

He said the EU decision provided the transition period required by state-owned Telecom Eireann to restructure its operations and efficiency while at the same time setting out the road to free and open competition in Irish telecommunications.

Earlier this year, Telecom Eireann agreed a strategic alliance with Telia of Sweden and Koninklijke PTT Nederland. Lowry said the alliance was a key element in enabling Ireland to meet the earlier liberalisation dates proposed.
